skim: Flávio Bolsonaro stunned incumbent President Lula 47.2%-44.9% in Brazil’s first-round vote, forcing an Oct 25 runoff, as France shut hundreds of schools amid student unrest and Catalonia’s storm toll rose to three dead.

Ethiopian federal forces retook Tigray capital Mekelle as the TPLF withdrew, Trump said Iran is “ready to fold up” as more US warships steamed to the Gulf, and Gaza’s post-ceasefire toll topped 1,446 after fresh weekend strikes.

OPEC+ held oil output steady for November as Brent settled near $102, Wall Street rallied on a weak jobs report that slashed Fed rate-hike odds, and Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon while locking it to cybersecurity partners.

Max Verstappen won a rain-hit Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia for Red Bull’s first victory of the season, Erling Haaland limped off injured for Portugal, and Marnus Labuschagne ended a three-year century drought ahead of the Durban Test.

Mumbai police booked 500 SIR protesters as India’s opposition demanded the Election Commissioner’s resignation, UK diesel prices were set to ease after an emergency European supply deal, and Qatar’s Amir was invited to the GCC-EU summit.

stories.headline: Bolsonaro’s son stuns Lula in Brazil’s first round, forcing Oct. 25 runoff
stories.body: With 99% of ballots counted, Flávio Bolsonaro topped incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva 47.2% to 44.9% in Brazil’s first-round vote — a result pollsters had not predicted — per Fox News (Oct 4). Bolsonaro declared “Brazil wants change, that’s the reading of what happened today. It’s the end of the Workers’ Party era,” while Lula vowed “Tomorrow we start a new campaign. I am very good in the knockout stage.” The two now face an Oct. 25 runoff after a campaign dominated by crime, corruption and Trump-aligned politics.

stories.headline: France shuts hundreds of schools as student protests near 5,000 arrests
stories.body: Some 400 to 500 French secondary schools were fully or partially closed Monday as a week of student unrest over unsafe buildings, overcrowding and staff shortages intensified, with 24 schools burned or vandalized and 78 education staff injured, per Euronews (Oct 4). Nearly 5,000 people have been arrested since protests began, and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez insisted “the police do not repress young people” even as reports surfaced of a teacher doused in petrol and a protester blinded in one eye. Teachers’ unions backed a planned “Act III” mobilization for Tuesday, deepening pressure on the government.

stories.headline: Spain’s storm system shifts to Catalonia, killing two more as flooding spreads
stories.body: The storm system that killed a 102-year-old woman in Albacete’s Madrigueras days earlier moved north to Catalonia, where two more deaths were confirmed — one in a wall collapse at a Tordera campsite, another in a flooded Montornès del Vallès garage — with a third person missing near the Pineda stream, per Infobae (Oct 4). Catalan emergency services logged 4,196 incidents and nearly 5,900 calls in a single morning, with Barcelona province, Maresme and Vallès Oriental hit hardest and a dozen roads cut. Catalan President Salvador Illa warned “the situation continues being complicated, especially in the northern half of Catalonia.”

stories.headline: Congo tests pill to stop Ebola before symptoms start, as toll holds near 4,000
stories.body: With the Bundibugyo-virus outbreak at roughly 8,300 confirmed cases and 4,000 deaths since May, researchers in Ituri province have enrolled more than 250 of a planned 1,000 participants in a trial of Gilead’s antiviral pill obeldesivir, given shortly after suspected exposure to block disease before symptoms appear, per Arab News (Oct 3). ALIMA research coordinator Dr. Guilavogui Jean Paul Yassa said the approach “differs from a vaccine, which may take days or weeks to provide protection,” while investigating physician Dr. Jacques Zawadi called convincing frightened, grieving communities to take part “the biggest challenge we face.”

stories.headline: Atlantic’s rare hurricane-free streak faces growing Gulf threat
stories.body: The National Hurricane Center raised the odds of tropical development in the southern Gulf of Mexico to 40% over the next seven days, though wind shear from the subtropical jet may limit how long any system spends over open water, per Fox Weather (Oct 4). The Atlantic has now gone 338 days without a hurricane, including the first hurricane-free September in 32 years — a storm-free 2026 would be just the third such season since 1914. Forecasters say any system would have only a narrow window between Mexico’s central coast and the U.S. Gulf Coast to strengthen.

stories.headline: Verstappen wins wild, rain-hit Bahrain GP in Malaysia for Red Bull’s first victory of 2026
stories.body: Max Verstappen converted pole position into Red Bull’s first win of the 2026 season, recovering from an early slip behind the Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell at Turn 1 to control a safety-car-interrupted, rain-to-dry thriller at Sepang. Antonelli held on for second to extend his championship lead, while Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc carved through the field from slick tyres to finish third and fourth; Russell’s race ended in heartbreak as he “ground to a halt on the start/finish straight” behind the final safety car, scoring no points, per Formula1.com (Oct 4).

stories.headline: Erling Haaland limps off in Portugal’s 2-1 Nations League win over Norway
stories.body: Portugal beat Norway 2-1 in UEFA Nations League action on Oct 4, with João Cancelo and Gonçalo Ramos overturning Kristoffer Ajer’s early opener. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland was substituted in the 67th minute after appearing to injure his leg on a close-range shot attempt, with Jørgen Strand Larsen replacing him and manager Ståle Solbakken greeting him with a hug as he left the pitch; per Sportsdunia (Oct 4), no official injury assessment has yet been released.

stories.headline: Marnus Labuschagne ends three-year century drought ahead of Durban Test
stories.body: Marnus Labuschagne struck 111 against a Cricket South Africa Invitational XI in a two-day warm-up in Potchefstroom — his first century in over three years — a timely statement before Australia’s first Test against South Africa starts Oct 9 in Durban. Opening partner Matthew Renshaw, who made 36, said: “It’s the Marn that I know that’s batting well. Really nice to see him getting the runs,” per ICC Cricket (Oct 5); Australia replied with 368/6 to the hosts’ 318/7 declared as the match ended in a draw.

stories.headline: UAE doubles charter fleet to fly fans to Gulf Cup final showdown with Saudi Arabia
stories.body: The UAE Football Association doubled its private plane fleet from six to twelve aircraft after every seat on the original six sold out to supporters travelling to Tuesday’s Gulf Cup 27 final against Saudi Arabia in Jeddah, per Goal.com (Oct 4). Both sides are chasing long-awaited silverware — the UAE last won the title in 2013, Saudi Arabia in 2004 — after the UAE beat Oman 1-0 and Saudi Arabia edged Qatar 3-2 on penalties in Saturday’s semifinals.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty snap 8-week losing run as Monday rally follows Fed rate-hike fears easing
stories.body: Sensex opened up 364–440 points (+0.5–0.6%) near 72,350 and Nifty topped 22,500–22,550 on Monday, breaking an eight-week losing streak as Asian markets rallied broadly — Japan’s Nikkei jumped 2.58% — after Friday’s weak US jobs report slashed Fed rate-hike odds, per Business Standard (Oct 5). Brent crude eased 0.64% to $101.57/barrel as West Asian exports edged toward pre-war levels, while the Reserve Bank of India approved Anup Bagchi’s appointment as HDFC Bank’s new CEO.

stories.headline: OPEC+ holds oil output steady for November as Brent settles near $102
stories.body: OPEC+’s seven core producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Oman, Algeria and Kazakhstan — agreed to keep their joint 31 million bpd quota unchanged for November, having just finished unwinding 1.65 million bpd of voluntary cuts while holding a separate 2 million bpd cut through year-end, per The National (Oct 4). Brent settled at $102.25/barrel on Friday, down nearly 2% on the week, even as the Strait of Hormuz — carrying roughly a fifth of global crude and LNG flows — has stayed “effectively closed since February 28” amid US-Iran fighting, with Iran’s conditions for reopening still unmet.

stories.headline: Wall Street rallies as weak jobs data slashes Fed rate-hike odds, Nvidia hits record
stories.body: The Dow rose 250 points (+0.49%) to 51,176.96, the S&P 500 gained 0.73% to 7,722.72 and the Nasdaq jumped 1.19% to 27,190.86 on Friday after September payrolls grew just 29,000 versus roughly 85,000–90,000 expected, with unemployment rising to 4.2%, per Yahoo Finance (Oct 2). The miss cut Fed odds of an October rate hike from 64% to 16%; economist Mohamed El-Erian said the data is “going to put the Fed definitely on hold for October,” while Nvidia touched a fresh intraday record on continued AI-driven demand.

stories.headline: AWS deepens $1B data-center pledge as $496B cloud backlog hangs on local fights
stories.body: AWS’s week-old $1 billion “Built Together” pledge for data-center host communities took on sharper financial stakes, per 24/7 Wall St. (Oct 4): more than 100 local moratoriums are under consideration nationwide against a $496 billion AWS backlog that is mostly committed to five-year-plus contracts. CEO Matt Garman warned that local bans risk the “US…writing its own losing ticket to this race,” as AWS’s Q2 capex hit $54.21 billion, up 68% year-over-year.

stories.headline: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon, its first frontier model in months — then locks it down
stories.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, its most capable model yet, but restricted initial access to cybersecurity partners in its Fairwind Program while it tests safeguards against cyberattacks and bio/chem/nuclear misuse, per TechWireAsia (Oct 1). Argon scored 68% on CWE-bench v1 and 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1, lifted maximum output to one million tokens, and has already helped Google optimize over 300 terabytes of internal data-center memory, with broader rollout to paid API and Gemini Ultra customers still pending.

stories.headline: Anthropic eyes $2 trillion IPO, warns investors Washington is a wildcard
stories.body: Anthropic’s confidential S-1 filing targets a pre-Thanksgiving, November listing at a $2 trillion valuation, per PYMNTS (Oct 2), while warning that “government agencies’ attitudes toward the company and artificial intelligence could affect its business,” citing Trump’s February order barring federal use of its models and Commerce Department export curbs on its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. With the broader IPO market frozen by 5%-plus Treasury yields, analysts told Benzinga (Oct 4) that Anthropic and OpenAI — flush with private capital — have “a luxury only the top two or three players have,” letting them time their debuts while rivals wait.

stories.headline: Altman: ‘The world should accept some bad things’ for AI’s benefits
stories.body: In a Politico Decoded interview reported Oct 4–5, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argued society must tolerate harm from AI in exchange for its benefits: “We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” He drew a hard line only at “a serious loss of control over AI systems,” and widened his rift with Anthropic by calling its preference for concentrated, tightly controlled AI development “a completely unacceptable trade-off” against OpenAI’s “lighter-touch” stance.

stories.headline: Anthropic’s bug-hunting AI finds a flaw — hackers weaponize it within a day
stories.body: Security researcher Zach Hanley used Anthropic’s Mythos model to uncover CVE-2026-61500, a critical authentication-bypass bug in Rejetto HTTP File Server, after Mythos determined that Microsoft’s Z3 solver could crack the software’s predictable random-number generator to forge session cookies, per The Register (Oct 3). Disclosed on a Wednesday, the flaw was already being exploited by attackers from a China-hosted IP against US and Japanese servers by Thursday evening — a reminder of how AI is compressing the patch window on both sides of the fight.

stories.headline: Ethiopian forces retake Tigray capital Mekelle as TPLF withdraws
stories.body: Ethiopian federal forces and the government-aligned Tigray Peace Forces captured the regional capital Mekelle after the TPLF withdrew, per Al Jazeera (Oct 5). The TPLF said it had “temporarily moved out of Mekelle” and would “operate from somewhere else,” while former Tigray Interim Administration president Abraham Belay said authorities are “working to establish a new administrative structure that will enable the people of Tigray to govern themselves,” with regional elections planned within months.

stories.headline: Trump says Iran “ready to fold up” as more US warships steam toward Gulf
stories.body: President Trump said Iran “is ready to fold up” and predicted the war “will be very quickly ended,” possibly “before the election,” while keeping open the option of resuming strikes after the Nov. 3 midterms, per CBS News (Oct 4). Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly asked Iran’s UN delegation to leave a day early after talks stalled, as three more US Navy ships carrying over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — including the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group — head to the Middle East, potentially putting three carrier groups and 20,000-plus troops in the region by late October.

stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv bridge again as Germany’s Merz arrives to sirens and explosions
stories.body: A Russian strike hit Kyiv’s Northern Bridge over the Dnipro on Sunday — the second bridge struck in the capital that weekend — damaging the roadway and cutting hot water supply, per Al Jazeera (Oct 4). German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made an unannounced visit to Kyiv hours later, announcing a $1.1 billion military aid package and $394 million for energy repairs and warning “if Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us,” while Zelenskyy said residents face “terrible nights and days.”

stories.headline: Gaza death toll since ceasefire tops 1,446 after fresh weekend strikes
stories.body: Israeli strikes killed at least five people, including four women, in a Gaza City apartment building on Saturday, and one more in a vehicle attack in Deir al-Balah on Sunday that injured 10, per The National (Oct 4). The Palestinian toll since the October 2025 ceasefire has reached 1,446 killed and more than 5,060 injured, with relative Fouad Al Najjar saying “today is essentially the worst day of my life. I lost my mother and my grandmother today.”

stories.headline: RSF accused of executing 25-plus civilians in North Kordofan as Sudan’s army presses offensive
stories.body: The Sudan Doctors Network said RSF fighters killed more than 25 civilians in the Umm Badr area of North Kordofan, citing video showing “RSF members executing civilians” in what it called apparently ethnically motivated killings of people accused of supporting the army, per Anews (Oct 3). Sudan’s army, fresh off capturing the al-Mazroub stronghold, said it also made gains against RSF and allied SPLM-N forces in Blue Nile state’s Minza and Bashkarkad areas, per Al Jazeera (Oct 4).

fixtures.headline: Gulf Cup 27 Final: Saudi Arabia v UAE
fixtures.body: The hosts and the UAE meet at Alinma Stadium in Jeddah, both chasing their first Gulf Cup title in over a decade.

fixtures.headline: India v West Indies, five-match T20I series
fixtures.body: India host West Indies for five T20Is opening in Lucknow on Oct 6 and running through Ranchi, Indore and Hyderabad before closing in Bengaluru on Oct 17.

fixtures.headline: Australia’s tour of South Africa, 1st Test
fixtures.body: Australia open their South Africa tour with the first Test in Durban, with Marnus Labuschagne’s warm-up century easing selection concerns after injuries to Josh Inglis and Cameron Green.

fixtures.headline: Singapore Grand Prix
fixtures.body: Formula 1 returns to the Marina Bay street circuit for the night race in Singapore, with qualifying on Oct 10 and the Grand Prix on Oct 11.

fixtures.headline: UEFA Champions League, Matchday 2
fixtures.body: The league phase continues with Arsenal v Lille and Atletico Madrid v Manchester United on Oct 13, then Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain, Roma v Real Madrid and Barcelona v Galatasaray on Oct 14.

portfolio.headline: Tesla posts its strongest Q3 delivery beat in years
portfolio.body: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating consensus estimates by roughly 25,000 units, with the Model 3 and Model Y accounting for 478,237 of the total, per The Motley Fool (Oct 2). The beat signalled sustained demand even after the U.S. EV tax credit expired, extending the Model Y’s run as the world’s best-selling car through three consecutive years.

portfolio.headline: Oracle lands $7 billion AI compute deal with Tencent
portfolio.body: Oracle signed a five-year, $7 billion agreement giving Tencent access to roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips hosted across Oracle data centres in Southeast Asia, with about 30% of the contract value paid upfront, per Tradingpedia, citing the Financial Times (Oct 1). Described as Tencent’s largest-ever overseas compute agreement, the deal adds to a cloud backlog that stood at $664 billion in remaining performance obligations as of late August.

portfolio.headline: Arm’s CFO lifts the long-term outlook for its AI data-centre chips
portfolio.body: Arm executives raised the long-term outlook for the company’s in-house AI data-centre processors, with Street fiscal-2031 revenue estimates for the business roughly doubling since December to about $26 billion from $12 billion — one analyst citing $15 billion of AGI CPU revenue expected that year — per TIKR (Oct 4). CFO Jason Child said first-generation AGI CPU gross margin should land in the “high 30% range, maybe low 40s,” improving toward 50% within a couple of years, while guiding fiscal 2027 royalty growth to the “high teens” as licensees shift to higher-royalty Armv9 designs.

portfolio.headline: HDFC Bank’s Q2 update shows advances and deposits both accelerating
portfolio.body: HDFC Bank’s provisional business update for the September quarter showed period-end advances of ₹33,075 billion, up 15.3% year-on-year, and period-end deposits of ₹33,275 billion, up 18.8%, with CASA deposits up 10.7%, per a bourse-filing summary (Oct 4). The bank also said it mobilised $11.5 billion via the RBI’s FCNR(B) swap facility and issued $2.5 billion in senior unsecured bonds between June and August to bolster liquidity ahead of its October 17 results.

portfolio.headline: HSBC downgrades Twilio over Meta Muse AI revenue doubts
portfolio.body: HSBC cut Twilio to Reduce from Hold while keeping its price target at $211, arguing the stock has run ahead of the revenue it can realistically capture from Meta’s Muse AI assistant, per Gurufocus and Ad Hoc News (Oct 4). The bank estimated Muse-related traffic would add only about $49.2 million — roughly 0.8% of Twilio’s projected 2026 revenue — since Twilio’s role would likely be confined to commoditized call-routing and verification services Meta could source elsewhere.

portfolio.headline: Fubo launches a regional sports add-on as Wedbush stays bullish
portfolio.body: Fubo introduced “My Local Sports” on September 29, letting subscribers in select markets add regional sports networks to a Fubo Sports subscription, per Ad Hoc News (Oct 1). Wedbush maintained an Outperform rating and a $19 price target on the launch — the high end of a ten-analyst range running $15 to $19.

stories.headline: Mumbai Police book 500 protesters as India bloc marches over CEC resignation demand
stories.body: Mumbai Police filed an FIR against roughly 500 people from the Cockroach Janta Party over Friday’s unauthorised Shivaji Park rally, while Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Uddhav Thackeray led a Saturday India-bloc march from Metro Cinema to BMC headquarters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over the SIR exercise, per India TV (Oct 4). P. Chidambaram said “the protests would continue until the CEC resigned,” while Asaduddin Owaisi alleged “people associated with the BJP and RSS were filing Form 7 applications to get voters’ names removed from electoral rolls.”

stories.headline: Swiss President Parmelin arrives for state visit as Modi hosts talks on trade and EFTA pact
stories.body: Swiss President Guy Parmelin began a three-day state visit to India on Oct 5 at PM Modi’s invitation — his first state visit and second India trip this year — with bilateral talks covering “trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, mobility, culture and people-to-people contact,” per the MEA (Oct 1). The visit culminates in the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on Oct 7, marking one year since the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) took effect, with Switzerland noted as India’s largest EFTA trade and investment partner.

stories.headline: India and Pakistan trade diplomatic protests over deadly Ferozepur border incident
stories.body: India and Pakistan summoned each other’s top diplomats on Oct 3 after two people were killed Oct 2 when Indian Border Security Force personnel engaged three individuals who crossed into the Ferozepur sector of Punjab despite repeated warnings, per The Print (Oct 3). Pakistan accused India of using “unprovoked lethal force” against unarmed civilians and said it “categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterize the deceased as ‘infiltrators,’” while New Delhi dismissed the claims as “baseless and motivated” and said the men posed an imminent security threat linked to cross-border narcotics networks.

stories.headline: UK diesel prices set to ease as Europe agrees to release emergency stockpiles
stories.body: Europe and the US agreed to boost diesel supplies to Britain in exchange for American guarantees to keep fuelling the continent, with prices — which hit a record above £2 a litre and have risen 57.6p since the US-Iran war began in late February — expected to fall “in the coming weeks,” per Daily Business Group (Oct 3). The RAC’s Simon Williams warned “households will be tightening the purse strings, while businesses may have no option but to pass these additional costs on to customers,” and GMB’s Gary Smith blasted the response as “sticking-plaster politics… not credible.”

stories.headline: RAF Fairford terror suspect released on bail as Westminster searches conclude
stories.body: Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed the 27-year-old dual UK-Iranian national arrested Oct 1 in Westminster under the Terrorism Act over the RAF Fairford incident has been released on bail with no charges filed, per a Counter Terrorism Policing statement (Oct 3). Property searches in the Westminster area have now concluded, though the investigation into the Sept 27 incident at the US-run airbase remains ongoing.

stories.headline: Qatar’s Amir invited by Saudi King to second GCC-EU summit
stories.body: Saudi Arabia’s King Salman sent Qatar’s Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani a written invitation to the second GCC-EU summit, delivered by the Saudi Ambassador during a Sunday morning meeting at Lusail Palace, per The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 4). The two sides also discussed strengthening bilateral relations between Doha and Riyadh ahead of the summit, which the EU has said it aims to hold in Saudi Arabia this month.

stories.headline: Qatar condemns Israeli completion of ‘Sufa 53’ line in Syrian territory
stories.body: Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned Israel’s completion of work on the so-called “Sufa 53” line in Syria, calling it “a flagrant violation of the sovereignty of the brotherly Syrian Arab Republic, a brazen breach of the principles of international law, and a grave threat to regional security,” per The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 4). Doha urged the international community to “compel the Israeli occupation to comply with the resolutions of international legitimacy, particularly the ceasefire agreement signed in 1974,” reaffirming support for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition dismisses Houthi claim of Riyadh/Aramco strike as ‘misleading’
stories.body: The Saudi-led Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen dismissed Thursday’s Houthi claim of striking an Aramco facility in Riyadh as misleading, with spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki saying the group fabricated the claim to divert from heavy losses — reportedly around 5,000 Houthi fighters in a week — amid Yemeni forces’ 257 precision operations against Houthi positions, per Arab News (Oct 3). Neither Aramco nor the Saudi government has independently confirmed any strike on the Riyadh facility.

doha_events.headline: CardzCon brings Qatar’s first trading-card convention to Sheraton Grand Doha
doha_events.body: CardzCon 2026, billed as Qatar’s first large-scale trading card and collectibles convention, runs October 9–10 at the Sheraton Grand Doha with more than 70 international vendors, live activations, and trading sessions. Gates open at 3pm on Oct 9 and 12pm on Oct 10, with one-day tickets from QAR 15 for children (adults QAR 25) and a two-day pass at QAR 45; under-5s go free, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 28).

doha_events.headline: Ramy Sabry brings his ‘romantic sound’ to QNCC this Thursday
doha_events.body: Egyptian pop star Ramy Sabry performs live at the Conference Hall, Qatar National Convention Centre, on Thursday, October 8, with doors at 7pm and the show starting at 9pm. Tickets start from QAR 595, per Qatar Living (Oct 4).

doha_events.headline: Majdoline Nasrallah’s ‘Witnesses Without Eyewitnesses’ opens at Katara
doha_events.body: Palestinian artist Majdoline Nasrallah opens a new exhibition at Al Markhiya Gallery, Katara Art Center, on Tuesday, October 6, exploring how everyday objects — blankets, cups, shoes, doors — carry memory amid displacement and loss, per Qatar Living (Oct 4).

doha_events.headline: ABBA Rëvival tribute band takes over W Doha
doha_events.body: A note-perfect ABBA tribute act, Rëvival, performs at The Great Room, W Doha Hotel & Residences, on Friday, October 9, with doors at 8pm and the show at 8:30pm. It’s an 18+ event with tickets starting from QAR 150, per Qatar Living (Oct 4).

doha_events.headline: Doha Players stage ‘Silent Sky’ at THIS Theatre, Mesaimeer
doha_events.body: Doha Players present Lauren Gunderson’s ‘Silent Sky’, a drama about astronomer Henrietta Leavitt, running October 14–23 at THIS Theatre in Mesaimeer. Tickets are available via Q-Tickets; specific showtimes and prices are listed on the booking page.
